content.title: THIS {{SIDE DISH}} QUIETLY OUTRANKS THE 'HEALTHY' FOOD NEXT TO IT
facts: A cup of cooked **spinach** has more iron than a 3oz serving of **chicken breast** — your body just absorbs it slower, so pair it with citrus to boost uptake.
**Swiss chard** packs more vitamin K in one cooked cup than a whole cup of **broccoli**, supporting proper blood clotting and bone mineralization.
**Avocado** carries more potassium per fruit than a medium **banana**, helping muscles contract properly and keeping blood pressure in check.
**Sunflower seeds** (1oz) contain more selenium than **tuna**, a mineral your thyroid needs to produce hormones correctly.
**Canned sardines** deliver more calcium per serving than a glass of **milk**, thanks to their soft, edible bones.
**Pumpkin seeds** (1oz) hold more zinc than **chickpeas**, a mineral your immune system quietly depends on every single day.
**Brussels sprouts** have more vitamin C per cup than an **orange**, even after they're cooked.
**Walnuts** (1oz/day) give you more plant-based omega-3 than **flax oil** by volume, supporting heart and brain health.
**Dried figs** contain more fiber per cup than **oatmeal**, helping keep digestion moving and blood sugar steadier.
**Mushrooms** left in sunlight for 15 minutes before eating can generate more vitamin D than a glass of fortified **orange juice**.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
Let's talk about a few of these swaps. Spinach's iron is the plant-based (non-heme) kind, which your body doesn't absorb as efficiently as the iron in meat — but adding a squeeze of lemon or a handful of strawberries alongside it can significantly boost how much your body actually takes in. Sunflower seeds are an easy one to overlook, but their selenium plays a direct role in converting thyroid hormone into its active form, which affects your energy and metabolism more than people realize. And mushrooms are the wild card here — they're one of the only produce items that can actually generate vitamin D themselves when exposed to UV light, almost like edible solar panels. Everyone's body and needs are different, so treat this as a starting point, not a prescription.
